content.why_desc: Unformatted SQL is nearly impossible to read, especially with complex joins, subqueries, and CTEs. Our SQL formatter adds proper indentation, line breaks, and keyword capitalization, making your queries easier to review, debug, and share with teammates. Well-formatted SQL is also easier to optimize and maintain long-term.

keywords.title: Keyword Capitalization

indent.title: Smart Indentation
indent.desc: Adds proper indentation to subqueries, CASE expressions, and nested clauses

minify.title: Minification Support
minify.desc: Strip all whitespace to compact SQL into a single line — perfect for query strings in code

optimize.title: Query Optimization

select.title: ✓ Avoid SELECT *
select.desc: Always specify column names instead of SELECT *. It improves performance and prevents issues if the table schema changes.

alias.title: ✓ Use Meaningful Aliases
alias.desc: Use clear table aliases in JOINs (e.g., u for users, o for orders) to make complex queries readable.

explain.title: ✓ Use EXPLAIN
explain.desc: Run EXPLAIN or EXPLAIN ANALYZE before deploying slow queries to understand how the database executes them.

index.title: ✓ Index Your WHERE Columns
index.desc: Ensure columns in WHERE, JOIN ON, and ORDER BY clauses are indexed for optimal query performance.

faq.a1: The formatter works with standard SQL and is compatible with MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQLite, SQL Server (T-SQL), and Oracle. Dialect-specific keywords are preserved as-is.
faq.q2: Will formatting change my query's behavior?
faq.a2: No. The formatter only changes whitespace and keyword casing. The query's logic, results, and execution plan are completely unchanged.
faq.q3: Can I format SQL with stored procedures?
faq.a3: Yes. The formatter handles CREATE PROCEDURE, BEGIN/END blocks, DECLARE statements, and other procedural SQL constructs.
faq.q4: How does minification help in applications?
faq.a4: Minified SQL reduces the size of query strings embedded in source code, makes logging more compact, and can marginally improve parsing performance.
